newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 recovers despite crown instability.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 recovers despite crown instability.

text.p: Czech major issues rebounded on Thursday but dealers said buying was mainly domestically driven while foreigners waited nervously for a resolution of the current crisis surrounding the crown.
The PX50 closed up 0.08 percent to 477.1.
Dealers said trading had been intense throughout the day with domestic investors taking advantage of cheap buying opportunities after several weeks of sharp falls.
Foreigners were seen staying on the sidelines pending the outcome of the current battle between foreign currency speculators and the central bank over the fate of the crown.
"Foreign clients are waiting to see if there will be a devaluation of the crown," said Ivan kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.
The crown has been under attack since early morning and the CNB has taken a variety of measures ranging from direct inetvention to closing off access to the last resort Lombard rate, to prop it up.
Towards the end of trading the crown was trading at around 4.0 percent below the mid-point of its mark/dollar basket from 2.5 percent at the open.
